options.description: Add a custom host-to-IP mapping (host:ip)
options.note: Python prints each host entry but does not shell-quote it (runlike-yak).

options.description: Add an annotation to the container (passed through to the OCI runtime)
options.note: Python ignores annotations.

options.description: Attach to STDIN, STDOUT or STDERR
options.note: Python only uses AttachStdout to decide on --detach and never prints -a.

options.description: Block IO (relative weight), between 10 and 1000, or 0 to disable (default 0)
options.note: Stored on create, but the container did not start on Docker Desktop (no BFQ weight support), so tests use saved inspect data. Reclassified 2026-11-06: docker create stores it on the Lima daemons, so it round-trips live.

options.description: Block IO weight (relative device weight)
options.note: Python ignores per-device block IO weights.

options.description: Add Linux capabilities
options.note: Python prints each added capability.

options.description: Drop Linux capabilities
options.note: Python prints each dropped capability.

options.description: Optional parent cgroup for the container
options.note: Python ignores the parent cgroup.

options.description: Cgroup namespace to use (host|private) 'host': Run the container in the Docker host's cgroup namespace 'private': Run the container in its own private cgroup namespace '': Use the cgroup namespace as configured by the default-cgroupns-mode option on the daemon (default)
options.note: Python ignores the cgroup namespace mode. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): stored only when given, so every stored value is printed.

options.description: Write the container ID to the file
options.note: The path is stored in inspect, but replaying it makes docker run fail if the file still exists; decide whether to print it or leave it out by default.

options.description: CPU count (Windows only)
options.note: Windows-only; the CLI refuses it against a Linux daemon. Live Windows round trip; the Windows daemon discards --cpu-percent when --cpu-count is set.

options.description: CPU percent (Windows only)
options.note: Windows-only; the CLI refuses it against a Linux daemon. Live Windows round trip (range 1-100; discarded next to --cpu-count).

options.description: Limit CPU CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler) period
options.note: Python ignores the CFS period.

options.description: Limit CPU CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler) quota
options.note: Python ignores the CFS quota.

options.description: Limit CPU real-time period in microseconds
options.note: Needs a kernel with real-time group scheduling; Docker Desktop refused --cpu-rt-runtime on create.

options.description: Limit CPU real-time runtime in microseconds
options.note: Docker Desktop refused it on create (kernel does not support CPU real-time scheduler).

options.description: CPU shares (relative weight)
options.note: Python ignores CPU shares.

options.description: Number of CPUs
options.note: Python ignores the CPU limit.

options.description: CPUs in which to allow execution (0-3, 0,1)
options.note: Python prints it when set.

options.description: MEMs in which to allow execution (0-3, 0,1)
options.note: Python prints it when set.

options.description: Run container in background and print container ID
options.note: Python prints --detach=true when stdout is not attached.

options.description: Override the key sequence for detaching a container
options.note: Only affects the attaching client; the daemon does not store it.

options.description: Add a host device to the container
options.note: Python prints host:container[:perms] for each device. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): class/GUID and IDType://ID values are stored as given and round-trip.

options.description: Add a rule to the cgroup allowed devices list
options.note: Python ignores device cgroup rules.

options.description: Limit read rate (bytes per second) from a device
options.note: Python ignores block IO limits; stored as bytes per second.

options.description: Limit read rate (IO per second) from a device
options.note: Python ignores block IO limits.

options.description: Limit write rate (bytes per second) to a device
options.note: Python ignores block IO limits.

options.description: Limit write rate (IO per second) to a device
options.note: Python ignores block IO limits.

options.description: Set custom DNS servers
options.note: Python prints each DNS server.

options.description: Set DNS options
options.note: Python ignores DNS options.

options.description: Set custom DNS search domains
options.note: Python ignores DNS search domains.

options.description: Container NIS domain name
options.note: Python ignores the NIS domain name.

options.description: Overwrite the default ENTRYPOINT of the image
options.note: Python keeps only the first entrypoint element and drops the rest (runlike-897, GitHub #141).

options.description: Set environment variables
options.note: Python leaves out image env values, but in stdin mode it repeats them (runlike-gjy).

options.description: Read in a file of environment variables
options.note: The file is read by the client; its entries land in Config.Env and come back as --env.

options.description: Expose a port or a range of ports
options.note: Python prints --expose for every unpublished port, including ports the image already exposes.

options.description: GPU devices to add to the container ('all' to pass all GPUs)
options.note: Stored as a device request; the test VMs have no GPUs. Reclassified 2026-11-06: docker create stores it on the Lima daemons, so it round-trips live.

options.description: Add additional groups to join
options.note: Python ignores supplementary groups.

options.description: Command to run to check health
options.note: Python ignores health checks.

options.description: Time between running the check (ms|s|m|h) (default 0s)
options.note: Python ignores health checks; stored in nanoseconds.

options.description: Consecutive failures needed to report unhealthy
options.note: Python ignores health checks.

options.description: Time between running the check during the start period (ms|s|m|h) (default 0s)
options.note: Python ignores health checks; stored in nanoseconds.

options.description: Start period for the container to initialize before starting health-retries countdown (ms|s|m|h) (default 0s)
options.note: Python ignores health checks; stored in nanoseconds.

options.description: Maximum time to allow one check to run (ms|s|m|h) (default 0s)
options.note: Python ignores health checks; stored in nanoseconds.

options.description: Print usage
options.note: Prints usage; nothing to recover.

options.description: Container host name
options.note: Python always prints the hostname, even the auto-generated one taken from the container ID (runlike-c77). Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): under --network host the daemon keeps the ID-prefix host name.

options.description: Run an init inside the container that forwards signals and reaps processes
options.note: Python ignores --init; the field is null unless the flag was given.

options.description: Keep STDIN open even if not attached
options.note: Python never prints -i.

options.description: Maximum IO bandwidth limit for the system drive (Windows only)
options.note: Windows-only. Live Windows round trip.

options.description: Maximum IOps limit for the system drive (Windows only)
options.note: Windows-only. Live Windows round trip.
Python never prints the static IPv4 address (runlike-bdg).

options.description: IPv6 address (e.g., 2001:db8::33)
options.note: Python prints the first network's static IPv6 address, whatever network it belongs to (runlike-bdg).

options.description: IPC mode to use
options.note: Python ignores the IPC mode. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): stored only when given, so every stored value is printed.

options.description: Container isolation technology
options.note: A Linux daemon accepts only 'default', so only Windows containers carry a real value. A Windows daemon stores its own default (process on Server, hyperv on client Windows); runlike leaves it out only when it equals docker info Isolation, so --stdin prints it. process and hyperv round-trip live on create; starting hyperv is untested (the test VM has no usable hypervisor).

options.description: Set meta data on a container
options.note: Python leaves out image labels but quotes values with plain single quotes, which breaks on a quote in the value (runlike-yak); stdin mode repeats image labels (runlike-gjy).

options.description: Read in a line delimited file of labels
options.note: The file is read by the client; its entries land in Config.Labels and come back as --label.

options.description: Add link to another container
options.note: Python prints legacy links on the default bridge.

options.description: Container IPv4/IPv6 link-local addresses
options.note: Python ignores link-local addresses.

options.description: Logging driver for the container
options.note: Python prints the driver whenever it is not json-file, so a daemon default such as local is printed too.

options.description: Log driver options
options.note: Python prints log options unquoted (runlike-yak).

options.description: Container MAC address (e.g., 92:d0:c6:0a:29:33)
options.note: Python reads Config.MacAddress, which the pinned API no longer returns, so a set MAC is lost.

options.description: Memory limit
options.note: Python prints the limit in bytes.

options.description: Memory soft limit
options.note: Python prints the soft limit in bytes.

options.description: Swap limit equal to memory plus swap: '-1' to enable unlimited swap
options.note: Python ignores the swap limit.

options.description: Tune container memory swappiness (0 to 100)
options.note: cgroup v2 daemons discard it with a warning (seen on Docker Desktop), so only cgroup v1 hosts store it.

options.description: Attach a filesystem mount to the container
options.note: Python turns every mount into -v, losing tmpfs, mount options, propagation and volume drivers (runlike-7p3). Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): bind, volume and npipe round-trip; tmpfs mounts are refused.

options.description: Assign a name to the container
options.note: Python prints the name unless --no-name is given.

options.description: Connect a container to a network
options.note: Python uses only NetworkMode and loses extra networks, aliases and per-network settings (runlike-bdg). Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): the default network is nat, left out; none, host and nat networks with aliases round-trip.

options.description: Add network-scoped alias for the container
options.note: Python ignores network aliases (runlike-bdg).

options.description: Disable any container-specified HEALTHCHECK
options.note: Python ignores health checks.

options.description: Disable OOM Killer
options.note: cgroup v2 daemons discard it with a warning (seen on Docker Desktop).

options.description: Tune host's OOM preferences (-1000 to 1000)
options.note: Python ignores the OOM score adjustment.

options.description: PID namespace to use
options.note: Python prints the PID mode when set.

options.description: Tune container pids limit (set -1 for unlimited)
options.note: Python ignores the PID limit.

options.description: Set platform if server is multi-platform capable
options.note: The chosen platform is stored in ImageManifestDescriptor.platform (seen on Docker Desktop); print it only when it differs from the daemon's native platform.

options.description: Give extended privileges to this container
options.note: Python prints --privileged when set.

options.description: Publish a container's port(s) to the host
options.note: Python reuses the first binding's IP and port for a port's later bindings (runlike-5id).

options.description: Publish all exposed ports to random ports
options.note: Python ignores -P and prints the random ports it produced instead.

options.description: Pull image before running (always, missing, never)
options.note: Controls the client's image pull; not stored.

options.description: Suppress the pull output
options.note: Silences the client's pull output; not stored.

options.description: Mount the container's root filesystem as read only
options.note: Python ignores the read-only root filesystem.

options.description: Restart policy to apply when a container exits
options.note: Python prints the policy and on-failure retry count.

options.description: Automatically remove the container and its associated anonymous volumes when it exits
options.note: Python prints --rm when set.

options.description: Runtime to use for this container
options.note: Python always prints the runtime, including the daemon default runc. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): none stored on create, io.containerd.runhcs.v1 set on start; both left out.

options.description: Security Options
options.note: Python ignores security options.

options.description: Size of /dev/shm
options.note: Python always prints the size, including the 64 MB default. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): stored only when given (0 otherwise), so every stored value is printed.

options.description: Proxy received signals to the process
options.note: Behaviour of the attached client; not stored.

options.description: Signal to stop the container
options.note: Python ignores the stop signal.

options.description: Timeout (in seconds) to stop a container
options.note: Python ignores the stop timeout; the field is set only when the flag was given.

options.description: Storage driver options for the container
options.note: Python ignores storage options; Docker Desktop stored and started size=1G. Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): size=30G round-trips.

options.description: Sysctl options
options.note: Python ignores sysctls.

options.description: Mount a tmpfs directory
options.note: Python ignores --tmpfs mounts, which are not in Mounts (runlike-7p3).

options.description: Allocate a pseudo-TTY
options.note: Python prints -t when set.

options.description: Ulimit options
options.note: Python ignores ulimits.

options.description: Set umask for the container
options.note: New in API 1.56; stored as a decimal number (0027 is 23) and printed back in octal.

options.description: Bind mount Docker API socket and required auth
options.note: Turns into a bind mount of /var/run/docker.sock plus DOCKER_CONFIG=/run/secrets/docker (seen on Docker Desktop); those come back as --mount and --env, the copied credentials cannot.

options.description: Username or UID (format: <name|uid>[:<group|gid>])
options.note: Python prints the user even when it equals the image USER, and unquoted.

options.description: User namespace to use
options.note: Python ignores the user namespace mode.

options.description: UTS namespace to use
options.note: Python ignores the UTS namespace mode.

options.description: Bind mount a volume
options.note: Python rebuilds -v from Mounts, prints anonymous image volumes, loses options and does not quote (runlike-7p3, runlike-yak, GitHub #138). Windows (live round trip on Windows Server 2022, Docker 29.9.3): C:\ paths, drive targets and named pipes (\\.\pipe\...) round-trip; the daemon stores binds in a random rotation of the given order.

options.description: Optional volume driver for the container
options.note: Python ignores the volume driver; only the local driver is available on the test VMs.

options.description: Mount volumes from the specified container(s)
options.note: Python prints each source container.

options.description: Working directory inside the container
options.note: Python prints the working directory even when it equals the image's, and unquoted (runlike-yak).
